candidates.statement: OpenHands CodeActAgent v1.8 with claude-3-5-sonnet resolved 26.0% of SWE-Bench Lite instances (0-shot, no hint text).
OpenHands' SWE-Bench Lite result (26.0%) sits within the range spanned by reproducible open baselines evaluated the same way (18.0-27.3%), rather than leading or trailing them by a wide margin.

0-shot, OpenHands CodeActAgent fixed 79.3% of HumanEvalFix Python bugs, above every non-agentic code-LM baseline shown (16.6-48.6%) but below a 1-shot SWE-Agent baseline (87.7%) that was given a full demonstration trajectory.
On WebArena, OpenHands' best configuration (BrowsingAgent v1.0, claude-3.5-sonnet, 15.5%) is below two of the four specialized/trained baselines shown (AutoWebGLM 18.2%, Auto Eval & Refine 20.2%).
On MiniWoB++, OpenHands' best result (40.8%) trails the specialist RL-trained baseline CC-NET (91.1%) by a wide margin.

On GPQA (diamond set), OpenHands CodeActAgent v1.8 with claude-3.5-sonnet reached 52.0% accuracy, above both few-shot chain-of-thought LLM baselines shown (29.6%, 38.8%) and above non-expert humans (21.9%) but below expert humans (81.3%).

On GAIA (L1 validation), AgentBench (OS subset), MINT (math subset), and ProofWriter, OpenHands' best configuration exceeds the comparison baseline shown; on the MINT code subset and on Entity Deduction Arena, it falls below the comparison baseline shown; on ToolQA, one OpenHands configuration (gpt-3.5-turbo-0125) badly underperforms a comparable-tier baseline while another (gpt-4o) leads the table.

The same OpenHands CodeActAgent, with one fixed system prompt and no per-benchmark modification, is evaluated across all three task categories (software, web, miscellaneous), whereas every comparison baseline agent in Tables 4-6 is evaluated in only one category.

A single, general action space (arbitrary code execution in a sandbox plus a browser DSL), instantiated once as a generalist agent, is compatible with competitive (though rarely top) performance in qualitatively different task categories at once, which specialized single-category baselines are not shown to achieve simultaneously.
No seed/replicate variance is reported for any of the 15 benchmark evaluations, so the numeric margins above should be read as single-run point estimates.

Cross-agent comparisons are not backbone-model-controlled: OpenHands is shown at several backbone LLMs while many baselines use a single, sometimes different-generation, backbone or a specialist trained model, so platform design is confounded with model capability in most comparisons.

The architecture and version numbers evaluated (CodeActAgent v1.5/v1.8, BrowsingAgent v1.0, GPTSwarm v1.0) are a specific, dated snapshot; later project materials describe a substantially restructured system (a separate SDK, 'V1' runtime, and 'Agent Canvas' front end).
The ethics statement's risk-mitigation claims are asserted, not measured by any benchmark among the 15 reported.
